description: A collection of segment-based representations of US public transit networks built from GTFS feeds, published on Harvard Dataverse. Contents: the description says GTFS spreads network information across many files and is cumbersome, so the dataset gives a concise representation as segments for over 550 US transit agencies. Version 3 (April 2023) holds 3,228 files: per-agency archives, 538 GeoJSON files, 538 PNG images and 538 zip files, and about 1,600 tab files. Producer: authors at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign (first author's ORCID given). Coverage: US transit agencies, all cities. Format and access: files downloadable from Dataverse (DOI 10.7910/DVN/SFBIVU), about 9.6 GB in total; free. Licence: CC0 1.0. Caveats: the page names 550 agencies while the Papers with Code entry says over 600, and the file counts match about 538; the underlying feeds change over time. Simulation uses: bus stop spacing and network structure inputs for transit accessibility, capacity and agent-based mobility models. Related records: none identified.
